synopsis: GSN structures a safety argument as contextualized goals decomposed through strategies into subclaims and evidence; the booklet identifies GSN Community Standard version 3 (2021) as its current definition [f9705, f12251]. SACM instead defines the underlying assurance-case data model, enabling exchange across tools and links to requirements and test databases rather than prescribing a drawing style [f12253]. Across Chapters 10 and 12, the booklet recommends a structured simulation-credibility argument, a GSN or CAE sketch in the plan’s safety-scope section, and a preliminary argument in Appendix A; the scope section is allocated 1.5–3 pages [f8021, f10155, f10156, f10182]. The intended value is organizing what evidence must demonstrate and making the argument accessible to different stakeholders, not strengthening the evidence merely by drawing it [f12241, f12258, f12259]. The booklet found neither direct comparative evidence that notation improves heavy-machinery safety outcomes nor controlled studies of readers’ understanding, and warns that diagrams can make unsupported premises look persuasive [f9722, f9888, f9721].
